message.content:
In this repository (a Go project, github.com/usememos/memos, at /bench/repo), the data layer is the `store` package (`/bench/repo/store/`), which defines persistent entity types like `store.User`, `store.Memo`, `store.Attachment`, `store.Reaction`, `store.Webhook` (or `store.UserWebhook`), `store.Activity`, `store.Inbox`, `store.WorkspaceSetting`, `store.UserSetting`, `store.IdentityProvider`, etc. (check `/bench/repo/store/*.go` for the full list of exported struct types representing DB entities, excluding `store/db/*` driver internals and `store/migration`).

I need to determine: of these persistent entity types defined in the `store` package, which one is referenced (via `store.TypeName`) from the LARGEST NUMBER OF DISTINCT PACKAGES outside of the `store` package itself (i.e. count unique importing packages/directories, not just raw occurrence count)?

Steps:
1. List all exported struct types in store/*.go (top-level .go files directly in store/, not subdirectories) that represent persistent entities (e.g. `type User struct`, `type Memo struct`, etc.)
2. For each candidate type, grep the entire repo for `store.TypeName` usage.
3. For each type, count the number of DISTINCT PACKAGES (i.e. distinct directories, treating each directory as one Go package) outside `store/` and its subdirectories that reference it.
4. Rank the top two types by distinct package count, with rough counts.

Focus especially on server/router/api/v1/*.go (many files but check how many distinct subdirectories/packages, e.g. server/router/api/v1 is one package even with many files), server/, internal/, plugin/ directories. Remember: multiple .go files in the same directory belong to the same package, so count directories/packages, not files.

Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. content.text:
## Findings

**Methodology:** I extracted all top-level exported struct types in `store/*.go` representing persistent entities (excluding `Find*`/`Update*`/`Delete*` query-option structs, and the `Store` type itself): `User`, `Memo`, `Attachment`, `Reaction`, `Inbox`, `IdentityProvider`, `InstanceSetting`, `MemoShare`, `MemoRelation`, `UserSetting`, `UserIdentity`, `AuthenticationConfigState/Mutation`. Note: this checkout of the repo has no separate `Webhook`/`Activity`/`WorkspaceSetting` files in `store/*.go` (top-level) — those don't exist as of this snapshot, so they weren't candidates.

For each type, I grepped the whole repo for `store.TypeName\b`, excluded matches inside `store/` (and its subpackages like `store/db/mysql`, `store/db/postgres`, `store/db/sqlite`, `store/test`), then reduced file paths to their containing directories (Go packages) and counted uniques.

### Ranking by distinct external packages referencing `store.TypeName`

| Rank | Type | Distinct packages | Packages |
|---|---|---|---|
| **1** | **`store.User`** | **7** | `server/auth`, `server/notification`, `server/router/api/v1`, `server/router/api/v1/test`, `server/router/fileserver`, `server/router/frontend`, `server/router/rss` |
| **2** | **`store.Memo`** | **6** | `server/notification`, `server/router/api/v1`, `server/router/api/v1/test`, `server/router/frontend`, `server/router/rss`, `server/runner/memopayload` |
| 3 | `store.Attachment` | 4 | `server/router/api/v1`, `server/router/api/v1/test`, `server/router/fileserver`, `server/router/rss` |
| 4 (tie) | `store.Inbox` | 3 | `server/notification`, `server/router/api/v1`, `server/router/api/v1/test` |
| 4 (tie) | `store.MemoShare` | 3 | `server/router/api/v1`, `server/router/api/v1/test`, `server/router/fileserver` |
| 4 (tie) | `store.MemoRelation` | 3 | `server/router/api/v1`, `server/router/api/v1/test`, `server/router/rss` |
| 7 (tie) | `store.Reaction` | 2 | `server/router/api/v1`, `server/router/api/v1/test` |
| 7 (tie) | `store.UserIdentity` | 2 | `server/router/api/v1`, `server/router/api/v1/test` |
| 9 (tie) | `store.IdentityProvider` | 1 | `proto/gen/store` (only — the field types are embedded via proto-generated `store` package, and actual `store.IdentityProvider` isn't referenced elsewhere by name outside `store/`) |
| 9 (tie) | `store.InstanceSetting` | 1 | `proto/gen/store` |
| 9 (tie) | `store.UserSetting` | 1 | `proto/gen/store` |

### Answer

**`store.User` wins with 7 distinct referencing packages**, narrowly beating **`store.Memo`** with 6. Both are core entities used pervasively across `server/router/api/v1` (the largest single API-service package, 22 files reference `store.User`, 16 reference `store.Memo`), plus `server/router/api/v1/test`, `server/notification`, `server/router/frontend`, and `server/router/rss`. `store.User` additionally is used in `server/auth` (authentication middleware/context) and `server/router/fileserver`, which is what puts it one package ahead of `store.Memo` (which instead has the unique `server/runner/memopayload` reference not shared by `User`).

Raw occurrence counts (not package-deduplicated) were even more lopsided toward `Memo` (150 vs 119 raw matches for `User`), which shows why the "distinct package" metric matters here — `Memo` usage is heavily concentrated within `server/router/api/v1`, while `User` usage is more spread out across smaller, more numerous packages (auth, fileserver, frontend, rss, notification) even though the raw hit count is lower.
